bush-tucker.name: Bush tucker
bush-tucker.summary: Native Australian foods historically eaten by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, including kangaroo, emu, and native fruits and yams.

fire-stick-farming.name: Fire-stick farming
fire-stick-farming.summary: Cultural burning practice used by Aboriginal Australians for thousands of years to manage vegetation, aid hunting, and increase biodiversity.

torres-strait-islanders.name: Torres Strait Islanders
torres-strait-islanders.summary: Indigenous Melanesian peoples of the Torres Strait Islands, ethnically distinct from Aboriginal Australians, known for a seafaring culture and strong traditions in sculpture and mask-making.

quandong.name: Quandong
quandong.summary: Common name mainly for Santalum acuminatum, a desert tree species valued especially for its edible fruit.

backhousia-citriodora.name: Lemon myrtle
backhousia-citriodora.summary: A flowering plant native to subtropical Queensland, Australia, valued as a lemon-scented spice.

tetragonia-tetragonioides.name: Warrigal greens
tetragonia-tetragonioides.summary: A leafy flowering plant native to eastern Asia, Australia and New Zealand, often cultivated as a vegetable; it grows well on sandy, salty coastal ground.

coolamon-vessel.name: Coolamon
coolamon-vessel.summary: Traditional Australian Aboriginal shallow carrying vessel used mainly by women to carry water, food, and babies, and sometimes worn as a hat.

dillybag.name: Dilly bag
dillybag.summary: Traditional Australian Aboriginal woven bag, also called a mindirr or bulbbe, used mainly by women to gather and carry food, especially in northern Australia.

kimberley-western-australia.name: The Kimberley
kimberley-western-australia.summary: The northernmost of Western Australia's nine regions, bordered by the Indian Ocean and the Timor Sea, named in 1879 after the Earl of Kimberley.

arnhem-land.name: Arnhem Land
arnhem-land.summary: A remote region of Australia's Northern Territory, named after a Dutch ship in 1623 and home mostly to Aboriginal Australians, many living in small communities with little Western influence.

x-ray-style-art.name: X-ray style art
x-ray-style-art.summary: Prehistoric art style depicting animals and humans with their skeletons and internal organs visible, dating back to around 8000 BC and found from Arnhem Land to Siberia.

sydney-rock-engravings.name: Sydney rock engravings
sydney-rock-engravings.summary: Aboriginal rock art carvings of people, animals and symbols found at thousands of sites around Sydney, some dating back as far as 7,000 years.

ku-ring-gai-chase-national-park.name: Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park
ku-ring-gai-chase-national-park.summary: National park north of Sydney, Australia, known for its scenic river setting and ancient Aboriginal rock art sites, declared in 1894.

lascaux.name: Lascaux
lascaux.summary: A network of caves in southwestern France containing over 600 Upper Paleolithic wall paintings, estimated at 17,000 to 22,000 years old.

cave-of-altamira.name: Cave of Altamira
cave-of-altamira.summary: A cave in Cantabria, Spain, with prehistoric charcoal and polychrome paintings dating from around 36,000 years ago, the first European cave art recognised as prehistoric.

the-dreaming.name: The Dreaming
the-dreaming.summary: Term coined by early anthropologists for the religio-cultural worldview of Australian Aboriginal mythology, an "Everywhen" when ancestral figures created the land; also used for personal totemic Dreamings such as the Honey Ant Dreaming.

national-gallery-of-australia.name: National Gallery of Australia
national-gallery-of-australia.summary: Australia's national art museum in Canberra, established in 1967 and holding more than 166,000 works, among the country's largest art collections.

pitjantjatjara.name: Pitjantjatjara
pitjantjatjara.summary: An Aboriginal Australian people originating from the Central Australian desert near Uluru, closely related to the Yankunytjatjara and Ngaanyatjarra.

malleefowl.name: Malleefowl
malleefowl.summary: Stocky, chicken-sized Australian ground bird known for the large nesting mounds males build and for giving no care to chicks after they hatch.

yol-u.name: Yolŋu
yol-u.summary: Aboriginal Australian people of north-eastern Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, whose clans belong to either the Dhuwa or Yirritja moiety.

songline.name: Songline
songline.summary: A path across the land, recorded in song, story, dance and art, that Aboriginal Australian belief holds was followed by ancestral creator-beings.

coalsack-nebula.name: Coalsack Nebula
coalsack-nebula.summary: A dark nebula visible to the naked eye as a dark patch in the Milky Way, near the Southern Cross.

murrinh-patha.name: Murrinh-Patha
murrinh-patha.summary: Aboriginal Australian people of the Northern Territory, whose homeland lies inland from the town of Wadeye.

wakka-wakka.name: Wakka Wakka
wakka-wakka.summary: An Aboriginal Australian people of the state of Queensland.

rainbow-serpent.name: Rainbow Serpent
rainbow-serpent.summary: A creator deity common across Aboriginal Australian traditions, associated with water; it gives life but can bring chaos when disturbed.

yowie.name: Yowie
yowie.summary: A creature of Australian folklore said to live in the Outback, with origins in Aboriginal oral history.

bunyip.name: Bunyip
bunyip.summary: Creature from the Aboriginal mythology of southeastern Australia, said to lurk in swamps, billabongs, creeks and waterholes.

william-edward-hanley-stanner.name: W.E.H. Stanner
william-edward-hanley-stanner.summary: Australian anthropologist (1905–1981) who worked extensively with Indigenous Australians, coined the term 'the Great Australian Silence', and helped shape policy ahead of the 1967 referendum on Aboriginal affairs.

mircea-eliade.name: Mircea Eliade
mircea-eliade.summary: Romanian historian of religion, novelist and philosopher (1907–1986) who taught at the University of Chicago and developed influential theories on sacred myth and ritual.
